candidate_archetypes.name: held-out verification harness
candidate_archetypes.template: Seal public smoke cases for discovery and reserve separate correctness, numerical, and memory cases for finalist verification.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: A candidate that appears faster under a weak harness may disappear after realistic numerical and memory constraints are restored.
failure_modes: Baseline and candidate use different numerical modes.
Visible tests let the generator specialize away required generality.
Latency improves by excessive temporary memory or invalid cached outputs.
implementation_recipe: Freeze baseline numerical modes, compilation settings, and measurement semantics before search.
Keep hidden or held-out shape/value cases unavailable to candidate generation.
Treat peak memory and prohibited fallback paths as first-class acceptance checks.

source.claim_scope: Evaluation study of LLM-generated kernels; use as a harness-design warning rather than a transformation recipe.
source.title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch?

evaluation_guards.title: Guard kernel search against benchmark and correctness reward hacking
validation_recipe: Rerun finalists on held-out distributions and adversarial numerical cases.
Verify that the candidate performs the required work and does not exploit harness gaps.
Report geometric or workload-weighted aggregate results with failures included.

candidate_archetypes.name: fission then selective refusion
candidate_archetypes.template: Split a compound stage into legal primitives, then fuse each primitive with the consumer that removes the most weighted materialization.

candidate_archetypes.name: weighted orchestration frontier
candidate_archetypes.template: Implement a small Pareto set spanning minimal launches, minimal bytes, and minimal duplicated work.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Removing launches and intermediates can shift the kernel toward register pressure or redundant computation.
Fission can expose better fusion boundaries while increasing the orchestration search space.
failure_modes: Greedy fusion creates a large kernel whose occupancy or instruction cache behavior regresses.
Fission duplicates expensive work or violates numerical ordering constraints.
A locally faster stage produces an incompatible downstream layout.
implementation_recipe: Decompose compound operators into legal primitive regions before selecting fusion boundaries.
Enumerate orchestration alternatives that include fission-plus-refusion, not only greedy adjacent fusion.
Score each alternative on weighted end-to-end latency and materialized bytes under explicit compatibility constraints.

source.title: Optimal Kernel Orchestration for Tensor Programs with Korch

matches.title: Explore fission before choosing global kernel orchestration
validation_recipe: Preserve an unfused and a greedily fused control alongside the selected orchestration.
Check every workload case because the best fusion boundary may be shape dependent.
Attribute gains to removed launches/materializations and record any duplicated compute.

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded architecture portfolio
candidate_archetypes.template: Give each distinct family one build/correctness/smoke attempt, halve the portfolio, and spend deeper analysis only on survivors.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Profiling should redirect search when an intended optimization moves the bottleneck elsewhere.
Portfolio-level progress can improve even when individual candidate lines terminate earlier.
failure_modes: The agent repeatedly tunes launch parameters after the measured bottleneck has moved.
Feedback is too verbose or unstructured to change the next architecture decision.
The search overfits a public anchor input.
implementation_recipe: Generate several architecture-distinct candidates before giving any one candidate multiple tuning rounds.
Feed compile, correctness, timing, and a compact bottleneck summary back into the next proposal.
Stop a local line after bounded failures and return to a different opportunity or architecture family.

matches.title: Use execution and profiling feedback as a bounded candidate-generation loop
validation_recipe: Track time to first correct candidate, time to first improvement, and best result at fixed wall-clock budgets.
Report correctness-plus-speed thresholds across all tasks or workload cases, not only successful examples.

candidate_archetypes.name: SM-scaled bounded grid
candidate_archetypes.template: Launch a bounded grid scaled by discovered SM count and process remaining elements through a coalesced grid-stride loop.

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded grid plus vector access
candidate_archetypes.template: Combine a validated bounded grid with the best aligned vector width only after both axes have independent controls.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Thread creation or per-thread setup may shift to loop/control overhead or insufficient memory concurrency.
Combining reuse with vectorization can increase register pressure.
failure_modes: The grid is too small to saturate memory latency.
Grid-stride loop control adds work without amortizing meaningful setup.
The persistent-vector combination consumes too many registers.
implementation_recipe: Implement a grid-stride candidate whose grid size is a small multiple of the discovered SM count.
Preserve unit-stride addressing within a warp and keep the monolithic-grid control.
Vary thread reuse independently from vector access width before testing their combination.

source.claim_scope: General CUDA design pattern; thread reuse and launch amortization do not guarantee lower latency for a memory-streaming kernel.
source.title: CUDA Pro Tip: Write Flexible Kernels with Grid-Stride Loops

matches.title: Use bounded grids and grid-stride loops as a thread-reuse candidate
validation_recipe: Measure enough work to expose reuse while retaining a small edge case that detects underfilled grids.
Compare bounded-grid scalar, bounded-grid vector, and monolithic controls.
Reject persistence when repeated loop overhead or reduced parallelism dominates.

candidate_archetypes.name: smaller-block latency-hiding point
candidate_archetypes.template: Implement a 128-thread point and compare it with the current schedule using compiled resource usage and edge-size timing.

candidate_archetypes.name: lower-occupancy ILP point
candidate_archetypes.template: Process multiple independent elements per thread while preserving coalescing, then test whether extra ILP offsets reduced residency.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: More resident warps can hide latency but reduce registers available for instruction-level parallelism.
Larger blocks can improve amortization while worsening tail waves or resource granularity.
failure_modes: The search maximizes occupancy as if it were the objective.
Block size variants compile to materially different register spilling.
The anchor size hides a partial-wave regression.
implementation_recipe: Choose a few block sizes that occupy different resource regimes rather than sweeping every multiple of a warp.
Pair block-size candidates with compiled register/shared-memory usage and active-block estimates.
Include an ILP or coarsening point because lower occupancy can still win when it exposes useful independent work.

source.claim_scope: General NVIDIA CUDA guidance; exact resource limits require official target-device evidence and compiled-kernel resource data.
source.title: CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide, Execution Configuration Optimizations

matches.title: Treat block size, occupancy, registers, and latency hiding as a joint frontier
validation_recipe: Measure the same candidate over anchor and edge sizes to expose wave and tail effects.
Record final register/shared-memory use and distinguish theoretical occupancy from achieved activity.
Stop when adjacent frontier points no longer change the weighted objective materially.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Movement stalls may shift to shared-memory capacity, barriers, or tensor-core issue pressure.
Interleaving can expose non-matmul dependency latency after matrix work is hidden.
failure_modes: Architecture-specific instructions are absent or compile to a different mechanism.
Extra buffering reduces occupancy enough to erase overlap gains.
The operator lacks enough independent work between producer and consumer roles.
implementation_recipe: Split producer and consumer warp roles only after identifying independent movement and compute stages.
Double-buffer tiles and express a concrete overlap schedule rather than merely increasing pipeline depth.
Interleave non-matmul work with matrix operations only when dependencies allow it.

matches.title: Overlap data movement and compute with warp-specialized asynchronous pipelines
validation_recipe: Compare an otherwise identical non-overlapped candidate and report GPU-active time.
Audit the final binary for the expected asynchronous movement and compute instruction classes.
Measure register and shared-memory growth and test edge sequence lengths.

candidate_archetypes.name: dataflow-fixed layout alternatives
candidate_archetypes.template: Hold tile dataflow fixed and implement coalesced, conflict-avoiding, and compute-native layouts as separate candidates.

candidate_archetypes.name: resource-bounded tile frontier
candidate_archetypes.template: Choose a few tile points that represent different register/shared-memory/parallelism regimes instead of a dense sweep.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Larger tiles reduce redundant movement but may increase registers, shared memory, and tail waste.
Layout changes can move cost between global coalescing, shared-memory conflicts, and compute utilization.
failure_modes: The search changes only scalar tile sizes and never explores a materially different ownership model.
A schedule wins the anchor shape but regresses weighted edge cases.
Compiler lowering does not preserve the intended tensorization or pipeline.
implementation_recipe: Write one canonical tile-level dataflow before choosing thread binding, layout, tensorization, or pipeline depth.
Generate candidates by changing one schedule axis and at least one joint schedule combination.
Keep shape guards and tail handling explicit so specialization does not silently narrow correctness.

source.claim_scope: A tiled programming abstraction evaluated across AI kernels; individual schedules still require target-specific validation.
source.title: TileLang: A Composable Tiled Programming Model for AI Systems

matches.title: Separate tiled dataflow from schedule choices
validation_recipe: Use the same dataflow and correctness oracle across schedule candidates.
Screen anchor and edge shapes before expanding the schedule neighborhood.
Record compiled resource usage so a faster tile is not mistaken for a universally better schedule.

candidate_archetypes.name: aligned vector4 interior with scalar tail
candidate_archetypes.template: Use 128-bit accesses only for the aligned interior, preserve a scalar fallback, and compare final instruction counts.

candidate_archetypes.name: aligned vector2 conservative path
candidate_archetypes.template: Use 64-bit accesses as a lower-pressure point between scalar and vector4 candidates.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Memory-instruction issue pressure may shift to bandwidth, register pressure, or tail handling.
Wider accesses can reduce instruction count without reducing mandatory bytes.
failure_modes: Pointers or offsets do not satisfy vector alignment.
The compiler scalarizes the access.
Extra registers or insufficient parallelism offset the instruction reduction.
implementation_recipe: Create separate scalar, 64-bit, and 128-bit access candidates instead of assuming the widest access wins.
Guard alignment and handle the remainder with a correct scalar tail.
Keep arithmetic and launch geometry constant for the first attribution test.

source.claim_scope: General NVIDIA CUDA guidance; benefit depends on alignment, instruction pressure, register use, and workload.
source.title: CUDA Pro Tip: Increase Performance with Vectorized Memory Access

matches.title: Use aligned vector loads and stores to reduce memory instruction pressure
validation_recipe: Test aligned anchor sizes and deliberately unaligned or non-divisible edge sizes.
Audit final instructions for the intended access width.
Record register use and achieved bandwidth because fewer instructions may still reduce parallelism.
